Subject: Stepwise commit schedule + SLA-triggered discounts (AWS Marketplace PO)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to share a short proposal for a stepwise commitment structure that maps to MAP milestones and ties in discounts that kick in as you hit operational SLAs. The goal is to keep the evaluation low-friction while giving Acme predictable economics as usage ramps in production.

High-level proposal (attached: 20261130-ben_map_draft.xlsx):
- Trial/Eval window (60 days): $0 hosted credits + 50k free inference units to validate workloads and latency.
- Pilot commit (month 3): 2k RU/month reserved (dedicated or marketplace PO) with 10% discount on list.
- Ramp tier (month 6): 10k RU/month reserved, 18% discount + 99.9% SLA for tail latency; additional 2% discount if 99.95% met for 2 consecutive months.
- Enterprise commit (month 12): annual commit with PoR pricing and a credit for one-time integration work.

Key MAP milestones we recommend including in the mutual action plan:
1) API integration + sample workloads validated (end of eval)
2) Security review signed off (SOC2 questionnaire completed)
3) Performance baseline validated (p95/p99)
4) Go-live and first production month usage

If you want we can route the purchase through AWS Marketplace private offer — that preserves consolidated billing for Acme and lets us tie the committed RU to a PO. I’ve looped Lauren on this email for the MAP doc and Rishi for pricing/commit details.

Next steps: Jane, can your team confirm the procurement timeline and whether Marketplace PO is required for procurement? If yes, we’ll draft the Marketplace PO terms and a staged discount schedule.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

Ben / Lauren / Jane —

Confirming the discount mechanics and billing behaviors:
- SLA-triggered discount: 2% additional invoice credit applied retroactively for months where p99 latency <= threshold (99.95%). Credit appears on next invoice. For Marketplace PO we will reflect the credit as a rebate line item authorized by Redwood.
- Billed units: We charge based on inference units consumed. Prefix/KV cache reduces billable tokens for repeated calls. For predictable workloads we recommend a small warm pool and an autoscale policy that caps burst to avoid unexpected overage spikes.
- Overages: Marketplace POs can include an overage rate (list - baseline discount). We recommend a hard cap alerting policy and a step-down routing to a lower-cost model variant before exhausting credits.

I'll update the PO draft to include a rebate line for SLA credits and a simple overage table.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
